subject: Post-call recap: competitive eval + multi-region perf plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Green <michael@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: competitive eval + multi-region perf plan

Michael — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the evaluation you mentioned.

Recap (from our call):
- Goal: Validate production latency and cost for FinLytics’ real-time inference workload (short prompt, 512-token context, ~40 tokens generated) across US/EU/APAC.
- Competitors you’re comparing us to: AWS Bedrock endpoints, Google Vertex/Model endpoints, and Anthropic/other inference APIs via their hosted offering.
- Priority metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail variability, cold vs warm start, throughput under 10/50/200 concurrent streams, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Security/residency: data residency requirements for EU customer data; need confirmation on VPC/private deployment options.

What we propose as next tests (actionable):
1) Latency sweep (us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1): 1k requests each region, measure p50/p95/p99 for warm and cold scenarios.
2) Throughput stress: 10/50/200 concurrent connections for 30s windows; measure latency and error rate.
3) Model parity: run identical model weights (open model we already validated) across Redwood vs Bedrock/Vertex where you have access — same prompt set and seed.
4) Cost projection: run token-counted baseline (1M tokens) and project unit cost using each provider’s pricing + observed batching/throughput.

Files we’ll attach: a short benchmark template you can run and the sample latency matrix we’ll populate. I’ll loop Rishi in to schedule the tests and share the runner + credentials.

Next steps / owners:
- Michael: confirm test windows & provide any IP whitelisting (if you need dedicated endpoints).
- Rishi: will provide the test harness, scripts, and a Drive link to upload results.
- Vivek: to follow up on private deployment/residency options and required compliance artifacts.

If that looks right I’ll schedule the first run for Wednesday (us-east test) and share a Doc with the runner.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_benchmarks.csv (template), regional_latency_matrix.png (template)
From: Michael Green <michael@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: competitive eval + multi-region perf plan

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- For model parity: we will run the same open model on Bedrock and Vertex; for Anthropic we only have hosted access so we may have to adapt the runner.
- EU residency: need confirmation that EU-region requests never cross into US telemetry (audit log requirement). Can Vivek confirm the data flow for hosted vs dedicated options?
- Timing: Wednesday works for us for the US run, but our infra team is only available 10:00–14:00 PT. Can we aim for 10:30 PT?

One more ask — can you include a quick note on how Redwood handles automatic fallback when a regional endpoint is unavailable (we want to see graceful degradation semantics)?

-Michael
Michael Green
Sr. Platform Engineer, FinLytics
michael@finlytics.com

On Tue, Mar 2, 2026 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: competitive eval + multi-region perf plan

Michael — thanks, I’ll own the test harness and runner. Quick plan and what I need from you: 

Test plan (short):
- Runner: Python harness (requests + asyncio) that supports region-specific endpoints and concurrent clients. Will provide a Docker image.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization (where exposed), errors per second, token count and effective batching size.
- Comparisons: I’ll instrument calls to Redwood, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, and Anthropic (hosted) where you provide keys.

What I need from FinLytics:
1) API keys or short-term creds for each provider (Bedrock/Vertex/Anthropic) OR a schedule to run from your side.
2) IP ranges to whitelist for the runner (we’ll provide an ephemeral egress IP if you prefer).
3) Confirmation for 10:30 PT on Wednesday (2026-03-04) for the US run.

Behavioral guarantees / fallback note (short):
- Redwood routing: by policy we can route to regional endpoints only; if a region is unhealthy we can (a) fail-fast, (b) retry within-region, or (c) fallback to a configured secondary region/model variant. For this test we’ll keep fallback turned off for strict latency comparability, but we can run a secondary pass showing graceful degradation semantics.

I’ve attached the benchmark CSV template and a blank regional latency matrix. I’ll push the Docker runner + README to the Drive link Marissa shared after this thread.

Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_benchmarks.csv

Michael — 10:30 PT on Wednesday (2026-03-04) is locked. A few final notes before we run: 

- Drive + runner: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f/view (Rishi will upload the Docker image and README there).
- IP whitelisting: we will provide an ephemeral egress IP and a list of ranges by EOD today. If you prefer to run the Docker runner inside your VPC, we can hand off the image and scripts.
- Data residency: Vivek — can you confirm the hosted control plane will not route EU-region request logs to the US? If the customer needs full EU residency we can schedule a Private deployment POC where logs and control plane sit inside the EU region.

Next demo: once the baseline run is done we’ll produce a short comparison doc showing latency curves and cost estimates vs the hyperscalers, plus a second run with fallback enabled to demo graceful degradation.

Thanks — see you Wednesday.

Best,
